rule: Each row has one primary class: PARENT_THEOREM, FORMAL_TARGET, FINITE_EXACT_RESULT, FINITE_EXACT_TARGET, EMPIRICAL_CONJECTURE, or IMPOSSIBILITY_BOUNDARY.

rows.statement: Representational universality alone cannot establish an intelligence-specific morphology theory; a universal simulator can reproduce target behaviors without yielding a nontrivial ecology-conditioned developmental/resource prediction.
No unrestricted universal morphology/optimizer superiority claim is admissible under No-Free-Lunch assumptions; superiority claims must be ecology-relative and assumption-bound.

Broad neural function classes have universal-approximation and computational-universality results under established constructions, so neural representability does not establish neural morphology as uniquely fundamental or resource-optimal.

Symmetric bounded developmental compilation may induce an equivalence relation only under explicit closure and tolerance/resource-composition assumptions; otherwise use a preorder/category rather than force equivalence.
rows.attack: Find non-transitivity caused by accumulated approximation/resource bounds.

rows.statement: Current-behavior equivalence does not imply developmental equivalence.
rows.result: Two machines are identical on every input in the complete registered universe before experience, then diverge after the same experience because their update laws differ.

rows.statement: Multiple syntactically distinct inclusion-minimal generating bases can generate the same bounded Boolean function class with different compilation depths.
rows.parent_boundary: Post/clone theory and functional-completeness mathematics own the general Boolean structure.

rows.statement: Under the registered one-bit adaptive-transducer protocol, developmental signatures strictly refine current behavior: 4096 morphologies collapse to 4 current-behavior classes but 2884 developmental classes over histories of length <=2.
rows.scientific_value: Calibrates developmental equivalence as a substantially finer relation than current I/O equivalence.
rows.claim_boundary: The underlying function generation remains Boolean clone-style parent mathematics.

rows.statement: Minimum primitive cardinality need not minimize registered compilation depth: richer complete bases can have lower mean/max expression-depth cost than inclusion-minimal bases.
rows.consequence: Fundamental-basis arguments must distinguish algebraic minimality from resource optimality.
rows.claim_boundary: Tiny Boolean calibration; not a general machine-intelligence theorem.

rows.statement: Tiny neural forward computation plus a gradient-style update can be compiled from a frozen structured basis without architecture-labelled neural/backprop primitives and with explicit bounded overhead.
rows.required_residual: Cross-paradigm same-basis compilation with no hidden neural macro.

rows.statement: Production/rewrite learning can be compiled from the same frozen structured basis without a production-rule primitive and with bounded update/execution overhead.
Probabilistic generative/inference morphology can be compiled from the same basis, or a bounded obstruction identifies where explicit stochastic structure is resource/learning irreducible.
Programmatic/library-learning morphology can be compiled from the same basis without hiding a universal interpreter as a primitive and with bounded execution/update cost.
There exist measurable ecology/resource/verification coordinates for which the nondominated morphology frontier changes predictably between at least two non-equivalent morphology classes.
rows.required_evidence: Prospective phase prediction, disjoint ecology evaluation, matched strong parents and search-encoding controls.

rows.statement: Some mixed statistical + exact-compositional ecologies admit a hybrid morphology on the Pareto frontier that is not developmentally/resource-equivalent to either registered pure parent.
Finite successful morphology searches cannot prove unbounded future novelty or universal superiority without stronger formal assumptions.
A phase-diagram hole can be prospectively specified from known-parent frontiers and used to predict abstract properties of a missing morphology before neutral search.
rows.required_evidence: Known frontier map -> frozen missing-property vector -> neutral search -> parent-reduction -> disjoint replication.

rows.statement: Verified morphology-search history can improve the generator itself, reducing complete cost to the first admissible frontier morphology or improving phase-prediction calibration on fresh ecologies.
